svg.title: AWS: built today and planned
svg.desc: What BranchBook has in AWS today, and what the hosted demo will add after M6. Outside AWS, on the left: the Administrator, IAM user branchbook-admin, who signs in with aws login and gets short-lived credentials; GitHub, repository KatlehoKomeke/Appointment-Booking-System, with the environment aws-demo (main and v* tags only, no reviewers) holding the secret AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN, the workflows deploy.yml (every push to main) and aws-connection-check.yml (manual), and infra.yml, which runs the tests and synth with no AWS access; and, planned after M6, a reviewer's browser. The AWS account, whose ID is never committed, costs $0 a month today apart from cents of bootstrap storage. In us-east-1 (N. Virginia), built: the stack BranchbookAccount, deployed by hand by the administrator, holds the IAM OIDC provider for token.actions.githubusercontent.com with audience sts.amazonaws.com; the AWS Budgets budget branchbook-monthly, $90 a month, which e-mails at $45, $72 and $90; the IAM role branchbook-github-deploy, with sessions of at most 1 hour, whose ARN is the stack output DeployRoleArn, copied once into the secret and never printed; and the IAM policy on that role, which allows only the statements AssumeCdkBootstrapRolesOnly and ReadReleaseRecordOnly. Beside it is the CDK bootstrap stack CDKToolkit, qualifier hnb659fds, with its roles, assets bucket and ECR repository. IAM and Budgets are global; no customer data is held here. In af-south-1 (Cape Town), built: a second CDKToolkit, with the five bootstrap roles deploy, lookup, cfn-exec, file-publishing and image-publishing, an assets bucket and an ECR repository; and the stack BranchbookRelease, deployed by the pipeline, holding the SSM parameter /branchbook/release, Standard tier, which records the last deployed commit. Step A: the administrator runs cdk deploy for BranchbookAccount by hand; the pipeline never deploys it. Step 1: the deploy job in deploy.yml enters the environment aws-demo and signs in through OpenID Connect via AWS STS as the deploy role, with no stored keys. Step 2: the role assumes the af-south-1 bootstrap roles. Step 3: CloudFormation updates BranchbookRelease. Step 4: the job reads /branchbook/release back and fails unless it equals GITHUB_SHA. Planned after M6, dashed, in af-south-1, at about $82 a month before VAT: BranchbookDns, a Route 53 hosted zone for branchbook.co.za, which is not registered yet; BranchbookApp, with AWS WAF (a basic-auth gate, a booking rate limit and an /actuator block), an Application Load Balancer (HTTPS on 443 with an ACM certificate, health check /readyz), CloudWatch (the log group AppLogs kept 7 days, and 3 alarms to the SNS topic Alerts) and one ECS Fargate task (ARM64, 0.5 vCPU, 1 GB, in a public subnet, reachable only from the load balancer, its image in the bootstrap ECR repository); and BranchbookData, with a VPC across 2 Availability Zones, with public and isolated /24 subnets and no NAT gateway, Secrets Manager holding generated database credentials, and RDS for PostgreSQL 17 (db.t4g.micro, Single-AZ, encrypted, 7-day backups) in the isolated subnets. The planned request path runs from the browser to Route 53, AWS WAF, the load balancer, the Fargate task on port 8080, and RDS on port 5432 over JDBC with TLS and no RDS Proxy.

g.text: Today: $0 a month (bootstrap storage costs cents)
:5432 · JDBC over TLS, no RDS Proxy · after M6
